newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds static, trade shelved for elves.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds static, trade shelved for elves.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds were static throughout the afternoon and spreads were confidently stated "unchanged" by a range of market participants ahead of the Christmas Day holiday.
High-yielders were equally quiet on Monday with respect to a handful of trades shortly after the market open, traders there said. Prices were quoted flat to up 1/4 in general.

Dealers across both markets noted investors were sidelined amid two consecutive holiday shortened weeks. PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended a 1400 EST/1900 GMT early close for U.S. fixed-income markets on Tuesday.
All markets will be closed on Wednesday for Christmas. Next week will yield similar market productivity because of the New Year's Day holiday on Wednesday, traders said.

Only the most liquid of high-yield bonds changed hands at all on Monday, traders said, stressing those markets were far from active as it was. Trump Castle Funding notes traded up 1/2 point to 88 in early trade, while Trump Atlantic City Funding 11-1/4s also rose 1/2 point to 98.

"People really couldn't do much trading if they wanted to and so they just don't," a high-yield trader said. "You're going to see more of the same until the new year and then people have a couple of new issues set to go."

In company-specific news, Rite Aid Corp began a tender offer for the $195 million outstanding 12-1/4 percent senior subordinated notes of Thrifty Payless. Rite Aid completed the $1.4 billion acquisition earlier this month.

Back in high-grades, the market mirrored a lethargic holiday session with prices finding marginal gains as managers squared positions, analysts said. As in the high-yield market, desks were half-staffed and predictions called for tight ranges until January.
The benchmark 30-year bond closed up 1/4 at 98-28/32 to yield 6.59 percent. The 10-year T-note rose 1/8 at 101-4/32 to yield 6.34 percent.
